distinguishing_features: Active high-gradient magnetic separation rather than monitoring or inference from existing telemetry
Gradient-driven capture of ferrous particles directly within a flowing molten-polymer stream
Magnetic collection and discharge intended to avoid clogging a conventional screen
Quantitative ferrous-removal test with a defined magnetic-field and efficiency threshold
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent ferrous inclusions from contaminating recycled-polymer melt without fouling or repeatedly replacing a conventional filtration screen.
parsed.viable_reason: Although magnetic separation of ferrous material is physically feasible in principle, the written mechanism addresses only ferrous particles—not labels or non-ferrous metals—and the proposed visual inspection of output pellets cannot reliably quantify the stated 0.5 g residual-mass threshold.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying HGMS or magnetic interception to separate ferrous contaminants from a polymer melt is an established, routine design choice for a skilled engineer facing this filtration problem.
